answers.answer: SQLite is a SQL database engine embedded as a library in applications. Applications call its public C interface on database connections; repository users can also run the sqlite3 command-line shell. The Tcl bindings and testfixture supply another evidenced caller boundary for tests. No particular external application or deployed user population was established.

Principal components: public API (sqlite.h.in); tokenizer (tokenize.c); Lemon SQL grammar/parser (parse.y); SELECT compilation (select.c) and query optimization (where*.c); prepared-statement virtual machine (vdbe.c and helpers); B-tree storage (btree.c); transaction pager (pager.c); pluggable OS/VFS implementations (os_unix.c/os_win.c). The shell, Tcl binding, and testfixture are consumers outside the core.

C implements the core; SQL is parsed through Lemon-generated C from parse.y. Tcl supports tests and source generation. Unix builds use configure (autosetup) plus make; Windows uses MSVC and Makefile.msc/nmake. The amalgamation combines core sources into sqlite3.c. src/ holds core and separately named test code, test/ holds Tcl suites, tool/ generators, ext/ extensions. Public sqlite3.h is generated from sqlite.h.in; sqliteInt.h and subsystem headers are internal boundaries. Shell and Tcl bindings are outside the core.

For the selected one-step public-library route, execution begins at sqlite3_exec(db, sql, callback, context, errmsg), declared in src/sqlite.h.in and defined in src/legacy.c. The caller supplies an already-open database connection. This entry point is distinct from the CLI executable entry.

src/legacy.c implements sqlite3_exec. Its loop prepares statements, steps rows, obtains column names/text, invokes xCallback(pArg,nCol,azVals,azCols), then finalizes. The public contract specifies NULL pointers for SQL NULL, no callback when omitted, and SQLITE_ABORT when the callback returns nonzero; callback arrays/strings must not be retained after return.

Direct dependencies include sqlite3_prepare_v2; sqlite3_step; sqlite3_column_count/name/text/type; sqlite3VdbeFinalize (not a direct call to public sqlite3_finalize); database mutex/safety helpers; sqlite3Error, sqlite3ApiExit, sqlite3_errmsg; sqlite3DbMallocRaw, sqlite3DbFree, sqlite3DbStrDup, sqlite3OomFault; whitespace classification; and the supplied xCallback function pointer. Parser, planner, B-tree and pager are downstream, not direct calls in this function.

Supported source path: sqlite3_exec -> sqlite3_prepare_v2 -> sqlite3LockAndPrepare -> sqlite3Prepare -> sqlite3RunParser -> generated sqlite3Parser. The SELECT grammar invokes sqlite3Select with SRT_Output; SELECT code generation emits OP_ResultRow (the unsorted output branch is explicitly evidenced). Execution resumes through sqlite3_step -> sqlite3Step -> sqlite3VdbeExec. OP_ResultRow exposes result registers and returns SQLITE_ROW; exec extracts columns and calls xCallback. Dynamic boundary: the callback target comes from the caller, so an arbitrary application destination is unknown. Generated parser transitions and query-specific VDBE instructions are not a single fixed C call chain; the shown branch does not imply every SELECT performs a B-tree read. This is source-supported tracing, not a captured runtime trace.

An evidenced direct consumer is sqlite3_get_table in src/table.c: it calls sqlite3_exec with sqlite3_get_table_cb and a TabResult accumulator. The callback copies names on the first row, preserves NULL values, copies row strings, counts rows, and rejects incompatible column counts. The wrapper specially handles SQLITE_ABORT to propagate callback-side errors. Changes to row shape, NULL handling, callback frequency, or abort semantics therefore require reviewing this consumer. It is conditional on SQLITE_OMIT_GET_TABLE being absent; this is an evidenced consumer, not an exhaustive impact list.

test/exec.test contains direct tests exec-1.2 (comments/empty statements surrounding SELECT) and exec-1.3 (SELECT after a second connection changes the schema); both expect success and column-name/value output {0 {a b 1 2}}. Tcl command registration in src/test1.c maps sqlite3_exec to test_exec; that bridge resolves DB, transforms its SQL argument, calls C sqlite3_exec with exec_printf_cb, and returns the result code plus accumulated output. exec_printf_cb appends names and row values to a Tcl_DString. Thus the evidenced path crosses Tcl command dispatch into C, then the function-pointer callback. exec-1.1 uses execsql for setup; I do not claim its generic helper necessarily enters sqlite3_exec. Tests were inspected, not executed; exhaustive callback/abort coverage is unknown.

SQL enters as sqlite3_exec's zSql; NULL becomes an empty string. Each prepare_v2 call uses nBytes=-1 and receives zLeftover. prepare_v2 forwards through sqlite3LockAndPrepare to sqlite3Prepare. sqlite3RunParser tokenizes with sqlite3GetToken, sends tokens to sqlite3Parser, advances zSql, and records pParse->zTail. sqlite3Prepare publishes that tail through pzTail, saves the consumed SQL in the VDBE, and returns the compiled statement. Its bounded non-NUL-terminated input branch copies SQL and translates the tail offset back to the original buffer; exec's -1 route uses the original string. After finishing a statement, exec assigns zLeftover to zSql, skips whitespace, and continues; comments/empty statements also advance the tail. The unconsumed tail is a position in input, not a separate parsed statement or callback argument.
